title: A scratch recording session with Von Gammon on drums
summary: Frank describes a no-name, no-pay jam recording with Perranti, Charlie Hartman and Von Gammon, playing bass.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And Von Gammon was the drummer then. Yeah. Von Gammon and Von had a nose for money, boy. And as you know, Perranti, he wouldn't pay anybody. So he rang me up one morning over. He says, come on. He says, we're going to make a recording session. And I said, okay. So Von Gammon says, go ahead. Come on over there. He says, we'll go. No, no, no tune. No name. No nothing. I don't know. It was just started off. E flat. Start off. And Perranti started playing. And he had Charlie Hartman on trombone. And he had Von Gammon on drums. Oh boy, where's the rest of it going? You know, there's a funny thing. Oh yeah. Who was that piano player that... Joe Wolf? No, not Joe Wolf was the other... Might have been Joe. From New York?
He was from New York? No, no.
It was a piano player that used to work more or less by himself down back in those days. Could have been Joe Wolf.
